idiom_name: service struct owning trait-object (or generic) collaborators, composed at the binary's entry point
implementation_notes: Rust has no container, so the whole structure is hand-written and the compiler checks it: define one trait per fine-grained capability, have the facade struct own Arc<dyn Trait + Send + Sync> when the collaborators must be swappable at runtime, or take generic parameters (impl Trait / T: Trait) when the set is fixed and monomorphisation is welcome. The trait replaces the interface declaration and the composition root in main replaces the container; the facade method remains the coarse use-case boundary and the unit of work is whatever transaction object the repository returns (sqlx::Transaction, diesel's connection). Keep the trait-object form when several implementations must coexist (production plus test doubles); for a single collaborator the generic form avoids the dynamic dispatch and the Arc.
pitfalls: Async traits: the future returned by an async trait method is not Send unless the trait is declared with the right bounds, which makes tokio::spawn fail to compile; native async fn in traits needs Rust 1.75+.
Holding a MutexGuard, transaction or connection across an .await point either fails to compile (guard not Send) or deadlocks on a single-threaded runtime; scope the guard before awaiting.
Arc<dyn Trait> hides the concrete dependency graph behind dynamic dispatch; keeping all construction in main (rather than a global OnceLock service locator) is what keeps the facade testable.
